title: Three Shifts and One Short Rope
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：request　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 request 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the foreman ① made the request that no worker in the site would have counted, and he said the making was the whole of the shift. The ② request, meaning the wish itself and not the rope, ran three shifts and stayed uncounted in the book; a request, he said, is the only thing in a site that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ request in that site had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ request at the far ramp, meaning the load they kept for the children to lift and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A request, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the foreman said the counting is the part that fills three shifts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the request was the whole of the matter, meaning the need and not the wish. The ⑥ request, meaning the need and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; request, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a wish and a need. He said the need is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ request had become a line in a sheet, and the sheet had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ request of the whole thing, the foreman wrote in May, was one site and three shifts of counting; request, he said, is either the load at the far ramp or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ request I remember is the wish counted in the sheet, which closed in 1974 and is still counted as the quietest in the site. A ⑩ request, my mother said in 1976, is the only wish that improves by being counted; every request, she said, is a need that has agreed to look like a wish. She said the need was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 请求；要求（指工地里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 请求；要求（指那个请求本身，与短短的绳索相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the request 提出这一个请求
D. n. 请求；要求（指留给孩子们抬的那一车）
E. n. 请求之事（抽象总称，指一处工地的请求之事）
F. n. 请求；要求（指施工单里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 请求、需要（指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 需要（抽象总称，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the request 意为“提出这一个请求”，1967 年那位工头把工地里没有一位工人肯清点的一个请求做了一遍。
request 意为“请求；要求”，指那个请求本身而不是短短的绳索，它经过了三个班次而在簿子上没有被清点。
request 意为“请求；要求”，指工地里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一根短短的绳索。
request 意为“请求；要求”，指最远那道坡台的留给孩子们抬的那一车，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
request 意为“请求、需要”，指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个需要就是那件事的全部。
request 意为“需要”，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个请求，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
request 意为“请求；要求”，指施工单里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1972 年这一个成了施工单里的一行。
request 意为“请求之事”，工头五月写道，整件事的请求之事是一处工地和三个班次的清点。
request 意为“请求；要求”，我记得的是施工单里清点过的那一个，1974 年收工了，至今仍被说成工地里最安静的一个。
request 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，请求是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的请求。
